model: Blended NTA capitalization (P/B) + underlying-earnings capitalization (P/E) at cost of equity, sum-of-the-whole (not owner-FCF)

inputs.share_count_basis: Flat -- no buybacks (ShareRepurchases=0 every year FY2018-H1FY2026) and SBC is immaterial (HK$9-28m/yr against a HK$600bn+ equity base, <0.005% of shares); no dilution risk modelled.
inputs.net_debt_note: H1 FY2026 (31-Dec-2025) balance sheet: total_debt 103,175 - cash 19,529 = 83,646, continuing the deleveraging trend from FY2025's 93,298 (net debt/equity 15.1%) and FY2024's 110,866 (18.3%). NOT subtracted from either valuation leg -- both NTA (book equity, post-debt) and underlying EPS (post-interest) already net financing cost/obligations, so deducting net debt again would double-count it (see valuation_philosophy).
inputs.last_fcf_note: Not applicable -- this is an NTA + underlying-earnings capitalization model, not an owner-FCF DCF. Reported FCF/OCF is not meaningful for a developer with large, lumpy inventory (properties-for-sale) working-capital swings; see valuation_philosophy.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 OCF 38,080 less capex 9,087 = 28,993, shown for reference only; not used as the valuation base.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual, cash flow statement note (0016.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:9010), HK$9m; immaterial to this model (book equity and underlying EPS are the value drivers, not an FCF build) and included for completeness only.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 finance income, HK$371m (0016.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:7504); embedded within underlying profit, not separately added since this is not an FCF model.
inputs.units: millions (HKD, except per-share figures in whole HKD)
inputs.balance_sheet_date_note: Most recent EXTRACTED balance sheet is the H1 FY2026 interim (31-Dec-2025). SHKP's FY2026 annual results (year ended 30-Jun-2026) were announced 2026-09-10 and are reflected in this valuation via the qualitative headline figures in the Analysis JSON (underlying profit HK$22.85bn +4.6% YoY, revenue HK$94.19bn +18.2%, final DPS HK$2.93, total FY2026 DPS HK$3.91) -- but the FY2026 annual report has not yet been downloaded/extracted into this ticker's filings, so the FY2026 year-end balance sheet (net debt, book equity, NCI) is NOT available and net_debt/book-equity anchors above are H1 FY2026 (six months stale). This should be refreshed once the FY2026 annual PDF is extracted.
inputs.wacc_rationale: COST OF EQUITY, not WACC -- both value legs (book equity/NTA and underlying EPS) are already post-interest, post-debt flows, so discounting at WACC and then also holding book equity net of debt would double-count leverage. HKD cost of equity built as: HKD/USD 10-year risk-free ~4.0-4.3% (HKD tracks USD via the currency peg; most SHKP debt is HKD or USD-hedged) + ~5.5-6.0% equity risk premium for HK equities (elevated vs a pure US ERP given HK/China political and property-cycle risk) + a modest premium for developer cyclicality vs a REIT/utility, netting to ~10.0%. Applied as a SINGLE rate across all three scenarios (owner-fcf.md s7f principle: risk lives in the scenario cash flows/exit multiples and probability weights, not stacked a second time into the discount rate).
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable -- SHKP's leases (as lessee) are immaterial (lease liabilities ~HK$1.7bn against a HK$700bn+ balance sheet, mostly office/retail premises for its own operating subsidiaries); not separately adjusted in an NTA/earnings capitalization model.
inputs.nci_treatment: All NTA and underlying-EPS figures are on a shareholders'-equity-attributable / per-share-to-SHKP-shareholders basis, matching the company's own disclosed 'Shareholders' equity' (HK$617,851m FY2025) and 'Underlying earnings per share' lines, which already exclude the ~HK$4.5bn of non-controlling interests. No further NCI adjustment needed.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: dcf-methods/SKILL.md routes 'REIT / property trust' to AFFO/distributable-profit capitalization at cost of equity, and 'land subdivider, inventory-heavy developer' to blended NTA exit-P/B and earnings exit-P/E -- SHKP is genuinely both (a ~59m sq ft investment-grade rental portfolio generating ~57% of segment operating profit, PLUS a capital-intensive HK/mainland development pipeline that is the other row). Rather than split segment-level cash flows (SHKP does not disclose enough segment-level NAV/cap-rate detail in the filings extracted to date to build two separate legs), I used the company's own IAS 40 fair-valued balance sheet (book equity is a direct NTA proxy, since investment properties are marked to fair value every period, not held at cost) and its own 'underlying profit' non-GAAP measure (which explicitly strips the fair-value revaluation noise per the FY2025 annual, note 1: 'Underlying profit... excluded the net effect of change in the valuation of investment properties') as the two legs of a single blended capitalization model, following the same structure used for CDI.NZ (blended NTA P/B + earnings P/E, 50/50 weighted, at cost of equity, PV of interim dividends). This captures both the rental annuity (embedded in book equity/NTA and in underlying earnings) and the development engine (also embedded in both) without double-counting, and avoids a plain owner-FCF DCF, which would be meaningless here (FCF/OCF swings on properties-for-sale inventory cycles that have nothing to do with intrinsic value -- FY2020 FCF -2,764 vs FY2025 FCF +28,993, a ~10x swing driven purely by inventory build/release timing, not earnings power). First valuation of this ticker; no prior model choice to reconcile against.

historical_growth.eps_note: eps_*_cagr use UNDERLYING EPS (HK$8.24 FY2023 -> HK$7.54 FY2025 -> HK$7.89 FY2026 guided), the company's own fair-value-stripped measure, not reported/statutory EPS. The negative 3yr/5yr trailing CAGRs describe the FY2020-2024 HK property downcycle (underlying EPS fell from an FY2019 peak of HK$11.18 to an FY2024 trough of HK$7.50); FY2025 (+0.5%) and FY2026 guided (+4.6%) show the cycle has now turned. Base-case Year-1 (FY2027) growth is set from this inflection, NOT by extrapolating the trailing decline -- see assumptions.base.narrative.
historical_growth.fcf_cagr_note: Not computed -- reported FCF is not the valuation base for this model (see inputs.last_fcf_note) and swings ~10x on inventory-build timing alone, making a CAGR meaningless.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (book equity / NTA-per-share growth, the primary driver for the NTA leg of this model)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (+1.6%/5yr) diverges sharply from underlying-EPS CAGR (-5.7%/5yr) and revenue CAGR (-0.7%/5yr) -- but this is explained, not anomalous: SHKP's book equity is a slow-compounding, fair-valued asset base (ROE only ~3.7% on FY2026 guided underlying profit / FY2025 equity) that barely moves year to year, while underlying earnings are cyclical development/rental profit that fell through the FY2020-2024 HK downcycle and is now recovering. A pure growth-DCF reading of either series alone would mislead; this model deliberately runs both as separate legs rather than picking one.

base.narrative: FY0 (FY2026, year ended 30-Jun-2026) anchors: NTA/share HK$214.53 (H1 FY2026 book equity, most recent extracted balance sheet), underlying EPS HK$7.89 (guided FY2026 underlying profit HK$22.85bn / 2,897.9m shares, +4.6% YoY per the 2026-09-10 results announcement), DPS HK$3.91 (interim 0.98 + raised final 2.93). Years 1-5 (FY2027-FY2031): NTA/share grows at a retention-implied ~2.0-2.3%/yr (ROE ~3.7-4.0% x ~50% retention, consistent with the 9-year historical equity CAGR of 3.1% and the tighter 3/5yr CAGRs of 0.9%/1.6% as the fair-valued fixed asset base compounds slowly). Underlying EPS recovers gradually from HK$8.20 (FY27) to HK$9.40 (FY31) as the HK residential cycle continues to normalize (record FY2026 HK contracted sales of HK$38.1bn, above internal targets) and the new recurring-income pipeline (IGC West Kowloon anchored by UBS/AXA, Scramble Hill, Cullinan Sky Mall, ITC Shanghai/Three ITC) 'successively contributes' per management guidance over FY2026-2028 -- but Year-5 EPS (HK$9.40) stays meaningfully BELOW the FY2019 historical peak (HK$11.18), i.e. this assumes a partial, not full, cycle recovery. Dividend payout held at 50% (between the FY2025 actual 49.7% and management's stated policy of paying out based on underlying profit, with recent increases signalling confidence). Exit P/B of 0.55x is set only modestly above SHKP's current actual trading multiple (0.50x book, Sept-2026), reflecting continued deleveraging and cycle recovery but explicitly NOT assuming a re-rating toward 1.0x book -- HK developers including SHKP have traded at a structural, multi-year discount to NTA (family-control/conglomerate-discount, HK political and property-cycle risk, and questions over whether IAS 40 fair values fully reflect current transaction pricing), and there is no evidence in this filing set that discount is closing quickly. Exit P/E of 13.5x sits close to today's actual trailing multiple (~13.6x on FY2026 guided underlying EPS), i.e. assumes the earnings multiple holds roughly flat rather than re-rating.

bull.narrative: HK residential recovery broadens and sustains (mortgage-rate cuts continue, mainland buyers keep returning, contracted sales keep beating targets as in FY2026); the near-term recurring-income pipeline (IGC, Scramble Hill, Cullinan Sky Mall, ITC Shanghai) completes on schedule and leases up at premium rents given SHKP's flight-to-quality positioning (IFC/ICC occupancy already 91-98%); SUNeVision's AI/data-centre buildout (MEGA IDC Phase 2, completion 2026/27) becomes a visible earnings contributor. Underlying EPS reaches HK$11.50 by Year 5 -- back near the FY2019 historical peak of HK$11.18, i.e. a full cycle recovery, still not above it. Payout ratio rises modestly as management continues signalling confidence via consecutive dividend increases. Exit P/B of 0.68x is a partial re-rating toward (but still below) SHKP's own longer-run average book multiple, credible if the balance-sheet-strength advantage over distressed peers (New World Development's gearing crisis) starts to structurally re-rate the sector's best-capitalised name; exit P/E of 15.5x reflects modest multiple expansion as earnings visibility improves.

bear.narrative: The FY2026 recovery stalls or reverses: renewed HIBOR/mortgage-rate increases or a reversal of mainland buyer sentiment (geopolitical/trade tensions, capital-flow restrictions) cool HK residential transaction volumes again; mainland China office/retail oversupply persists and pressures rental reversions further; the new recurring-income pipeline (IGC, ITC Shanghai) faces slower-than-guided lease-up given a softer office/retail demand backdrop. Underlying EPS drops back toward HK$7.00-7.20 (below the FY2024 trough of HK$7.50) before a shallow recovery, NTA/share essentially flat for two years as retained earnings shrink. Dividend payout is trimmed (mirroring the FY2024 cut from 4.95 to 3.75) to preserve the balance-sheet strength that is SHKP's core competitive advantage over distressed peers. Exit P/B of 0.42x is a further de-rating below the current 0.50x -- plausible if sector-wide credit stress at other HK developers (New World Development's crisis) drags down market sentiment toward HK property equities broadly even though SHKP's own 15.1% net gearing remains sound; exit P/E of 11.0x reflects a market pricing in continued earnings uncertainty.

base.revenue_note: Not modelled as a separate line -- this is a book-value/earnings capitalization model, not a revenue-driven owner-FCF build. Revenue is embedded in the underlying-EPS path via management's own disclosed growth trajectory.

sensitivity.note: Base-case blended IV (50% NTA leg at the given P/B, 50% earnings leg held at 13.5x exit P/E) across cost-of-equity and exit-P/B combinations.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 25/50/25. Held at default rather than skewed: SHKP's balance sheet (15.1% net gearing, A1/A+ ratings, 6.0x interest cover) gives it no near-term solvency/refinancing risk (unlike sector peer New World Development), so the bear case here is a cyclical earnings/multiple setback, not a going-concern risk -- there is no basis in the filings to underweight it below the house default, and the HK property cycle's recovery is recent (FY2026 is the first clear up-year after a 5-year underlying-EPS decline) so it is too early to overweight the bull case either.
probability_weighted.band_position_note: No SBC adjustment applies to this model (house and street coincide since SBC is immaterial and not part of the valuation build), so band_position is not meaningful -- set to null per the house-vs-street convention for SBC-zero/non-FCF models rather than reporting a degenerate 0.

valuation_philosophy.summary: SHKP is valued as a blend of two legs, both discounted at the HKD cost of equity (not WACC) and both already net of debt/financing cost, so net debt is never subtracted a second time: (1) an NTA leg, capitalizing Year-5 projected book equity/share (a direct NAV proxy, since SHKP's investment properties are IAS 40 fair-valued every period) at an exit price-to-book multiple set close to SHKP's own current ~0.50x trading discount -- deliberately NOT assuming a re-rating to 1.0x book, because HK developers including SHKP have traded at a structural multi-year discount to NTA; and (2) an earnings leg, capitalizing Year-5 projected underlying EPS (SHKP's own fair-value-stripped non-GAAP profit measure) at an exit P/E close to today's actual ~13.6x multiple. Interim dividends are discounted and added to both legs. The two legs are weighted 50/50 and probability-weighted 25/50/25 bear/base/bull. This avoids a plain owner-FCF DCF, which is not meaningful here: reported FCF swings ~10x year to year purely on properties-for-sale inventory build/release timing (FY2020 -2,764 vs FY2025 +28,993), which reflects development-cycle timing, not underlying earnings power or asset value.
key_risks_to_valuation: FY2026 annual report (year ended 30-Jun-2026, results announced 2026-09-10) has not yet been extracted into this ticker's filings -- the FY2026 year-end balance sheet (book equity, net debt, NCI) is not available, so the NTA leg's Year-0 anchor is the H1 FY2026 (31-Dec-2025) balance sheet, six months stale. Should be refreshed once the FY2026 annual PDF is downloaded and extracted; the underlying-EPS and DPS anchors ARE current (from the FY2026 results headline figures in the Analysis JSON) but book equity/net debt are not.

The central valuation tension is the ~50% discount to book at which SHKP currently trades -- if that discount is permanent/structural (family-control governance, HK political risk, questions over whether fair-valued investment properties reflect current transaction pricing in a soft market) rather than cyclical, the NTA leg's exit multiple assumption (0.55x base) could still be too generous even though it sits only modestly above today's actual 0.50x.

Mainland China office/retail oversupply could deteriorate further and pressure investment-property fair values (and therefore book equity/NTA) even as the Hong Kong residential development cycle recovers -- the two halves of the business can diverge.

This model has no segment-level NAV/cap-rate build (rental portfolio vs. development land bank vs. SUNeVision/SmarTone stakes valued separately) -- SHKP does not disclose enough segment detail in the filings extracted to date to support that split; a future refresh with a segment-level sum-of-parts (particularly separating out the ~73%-owned, separately-listed SUNeVision at its own market value) could materially change the picture in either direction.

Cost of equity (10.0%) is a single estimate without a formal beta regression against HSI/HK property peers; a higher HKD risk-free rate or wider HK equity risk premium than assumed would lower every scenario's intrinsic value.
